clue.text: Cup drunk, alcoholic, round end of marriage, traditionally encouraged

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and jumbled, so the letters of cup are rearranged
round means the word for alcoholic goes around the other piece

parts.note: hard drink is alcoholic, so hard means alcoholic

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word marriage

parts.note: the word whose last letter is used

explanation.surface: A tipsy wedding guest raises a cup as the marriage ends, cheered on by the old-fashioned crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' gives UPC; 'alcoholic' is hard as in hard liquor, wrapped 'round' the 'end of' marriage for HEARD. 'traditionally' marks Spenser's archaic verb upcheer.
explanation.definitionFit: To upcheer is an obsolete verb for cheering up or heartening someone, so its past form fits.

clue.text: Husband occupying seat in church — that's a relief

indicators.note: occupying means the husband's letter sits inside the church seat

parts.note: a pew is a bench in a church

explanation.surface: A husband finally finds a pew in the packed church and sighs with relief.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection is an exclamation people utter when tension or worry suddenly passes.

clue.text: Outcry in the US, Democrats all upset — slated with this?

indicators.note: upset means the letters of 'Democrats all' are overturned into a new order

parts.note: the letters left over when the answer is taken from the anagram

explanation.surface: American Democrats are all upset, criticised harshly and making a din about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' works on DEMOCRATS ALL, which is the answer plus SLATED shuffled together. 'in the US' points to the American spelling without the U.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamour is a loud protesting shout from many people, an uproar of complaint.

clue.text: Bible brought in, pawned, vandalized

indicators.note: brought in means the Bible's letters are put inside the word for pawned

parts.note: to hock something is to pawn it
AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone pawned a church Bible and wrecked the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' puts the Authorized Version inside the pawning word. Havock is an older spelling of havoc, to lay waste.
explanation.definitionFit: To havoc is to devastate or ravage, which is what vandals do to property.

clue.text: Horrified as before at having to limit fuel

indicators.note: limit means hem in, so at goes around the fuel word

parts.note: gas is a fuel

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled at a rule capping fuel use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having to limit' makes 'at' the container rather than a link word. 'as before' signals an old spelling of aghast.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the archaic form of aghast, meaning struck with horror or amazement.

clue.text: Monarch retaining doctor as potato-peeler

indicators.note: retaining means the monarch word keeps the doctor inside it

parts.note: a monarch is a ruler
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A king keeps a doctor on as his kitchen's potato-peeler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retaining' has RULER hold MB. A rumbler is a revolving drum machine that peels potatoes by tumbling them.
explanation.definitionFit: The machine's rotating abrasive drum strips skins from potatoes, so it serves as a mechanical peeler.

clue.text: Sold drugs, vile trade involving change of hands?

indicators.note: vile suggests something debased and twisted, so the letters are jumbled
right hand swaps for left hand, so the R of trade gives way to L

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A drug dealer's nasty trade sees goods pass from hand to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving change of hands?' swaps R (right) in TRADE for L (left), giving TLADE, and 'vile' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal is slang for selling illegal drugs, so the past tense is having sold them.

clue.text: Traditional volumes found among faded daybooks

indicators.note: found among means the answer sits within the letters of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of faded and the start of daybooks

explanation.surface: Old books of tradition turn up among some faded diaries.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eddas are the Old Norse collections of mythological poems and lore.

clue.text: In the manner of noodles, soft, wrapped in paper napkin

indicators.note: wrapped in means the soft letter is enclosed by the napkin word

parts.note: a doily is a small decorative paper mat or napkin
P is piano, the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: Soft noodles served wrapped in a paper napkin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapped in' puts P inside DOILY. 'noodles' here are fools, not pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is a simpleton, and acting dopily means acting stupidly, as a fool would.

clue.text: Tea maid's prepared for natural gap

indicators.note: prepared means made ready in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The tea lady has made something ready to fill a natural gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A diastema is an anatomical space between teeth, such as the gap between front teeth.

clue.text: Latin bird in part of choir producing jaunty movements

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the choir section

parts.note: the altos are one section of a choir
an egret is a heron-like bird

explanation.surface: A Latin-named bird joins the choir and produces lively music.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegretto movements are fairly brisk, light pieces in a symphony or sonata.

clue.text: Intermittent

parts.note: the clue is only a plain definition: this is the word for Azed's clue-writing competition, which solvers are asked to clue themselves

explanation.walkthrough: Azed's competition puzzles give the competition word by definition alone, with no wordplay; solvers enter their own clue for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasmodical is an older form of spasmodic, meaning occurring in fits and starts, irregularly.

clue.text: Romance of a kind getting Dougie all excited, name secreted (10, two words, apostrophe)

indicators.note: secreted means the name letter is hidden within the jumble
excited means stirred up, so the letters of Dougie and all are thrown into a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges DOUGIE ALL into LAGUEDOIL, and 'secreted' hides N within it. 'Romance' means a Romance language, not a love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Langue d'oïl is the medieval French dialect group of the north, one of the Romance tongues.

clue.text: It helps to shift log rolling certainly round Virginia

indicators.note: rolling means the whole built word is turned over and read backwards
round means the word for certainly wraps around the state

parts.note: yep is an informal yes, certainly
VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: A tool certainly helps with log rolling around Virginia's forests.
explanation.definitionFit: A peavy is a lumberjack's hooked lever used to grip and roll logs.

clue.text: Dismay shown by the old man turning on mate

indicators.note: turning means the father word is flipped round

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, the old man
a pal is a mate, a friend

explanation.surface: Dad shocks everyone by turning on his best friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is a verb meaning to horrify or fill with consternation.

clue.text: Woman mostly in a bad way comes to us for charitable relief

indicators.note: in a bad way means in disorder, so the letters are scrambled
mostly means the last letter of woman is dropped

parts.note: the word woman itself

explanation.surface: A woman in poor straits comes to us asking for charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims to WOMA before 'in a bad way' scrambles it to AWMO. Awmous is a Scots word for alms, given to the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots term means alms, money or food given to the poor.

clue.text: Hardened clay, see, in grip of cold wind

indicators.note: in the grip of means held inside the wind word

parts.note: the bise is a cold north wind in Switzerland and France
la is an old exclamation meaning look, see

explanation.surface: Hardened clay lies, look, gripped by a freezing wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Blaise (blaes) is hardened shale or clay, used for surfacing sports pitches in Scotland.

clue.text: Polar vehicle? Steer from the rear, perched outside

indicators.note: outside means the perched word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to sit on something is to perch, so perched means sat

indicators.note: from the rear means the steer word is read backwards

parts.note: to con a ship is to steer it

explanation.surface: Someone perched outside steers a vehicle from the back seat.

explanation.definitionFit: A snowcat is a tracked vehicle built to travel over snow, as on polar expeditions.

clue.text: Headlong fall? Nothing to ease the pain at cut

parts.note: no means none, nothing

indicators.note: cut means the letters of at are removed from the drug word

parts.note: a sedative is given to ease pain or calm

explanation.surface: A patient is cut without anaesthetic, and the outcome is a plunge.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosedive is a steep downward plunge, whether by an aircraft or a falling price.

clue.text: Horlicks (more than one) — or Bells?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: blunders; making a horlicks is British slang for a mess-up
second meaning: things that clang, ringing bells

explanation.walkthrough: Horlicks is a British malted drink, but 'make a horlicks of' is slang for botch, so it means a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A clanger is a conspicuous blunder, and a clanger is also something that clangs like a bell.

clue.text: One manipulates accounts to mislead key filter somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A fraudster rigs a key filter to deceive auditors.
explanation.definitionFit: Kite-flying is raising money on fictitious bills or cheques, a fraud on accounts.

clue.text: Like a long run? Men should be dressed in a hat

indicators.note: in means the arranged letters go inside the hat word

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

indicators.note: dressed means arranged in line, as troops are, so the letters are reordered

explanation.definitionFit: A ten-mile run is a long-distance race, so the compound describes such a run.

clue.text: They emit foul smell — very large gauge reverse of ideal

parts.note: OS is outsize, the clothing abbreviation
a meter is a measuring gauge

indicators.note: reverse of means the ideal word is written backwards

parts.note: A1 is first-rate, ideal, written as AI

explanation.definitionFit: Osmeteria are forked glands on swallowtail caterpillars that give off a repellent odour.

clue.text: Sectarian, fatuous by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the answer is said like the fatuous word

parts.note: moony means dreamily foolish, fatuous

explanation.surface: A sect member sounds silly and dreamy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Moonie is a member of the Unification Church founded by Sun Myung Moon, a sect.

clue.text: Dog or kitten mostly excluded round small cooking area

indicators.note: round means the shortened kitten sat on both sides, so its tail is also taken from the far end
excluded means the first part of the shortened kitten is taken out of the kitchen word

parts.note: a kitchenette is a small kitchen

clue.text: Maori settlement dividing street up for NZ shrubs

up in a down clue means the street letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: utu is the Maori word for settlement of a debt, recompense

explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ST into TS, and UTU is 'dividing' it. 'settlement' looks like a village, but utu means a settling of accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutu is a poisonous New Zealand shrub of the genus Coriaria.

clue.text: One's produced in boiling haunts?

indicators.note: boiling means seething, churned up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.definitionFit: A sunhat is a wide-brimmed hat worn for shade, brought out in hot places.

clue.text: Theological student, one of two for tutor occupying comfy seat

indicators.note: occupying means the letter sits inside the seat word

parts.note: a sofa is a comfortable seat
tutor contains two Ts, so this is one T

explanation.surface: A divinity student shares a comfy sofa with a tutor.
explanation.definitionFit: A softa is a Muslim student of theology and sacred law in Turkey.

clue.text: Logical fallacy I mould deviously

clue.text: Syrup, golden stuff, grand to have for breakfast?

to eat is to have a meal such as breakfast

explanation.surface: Golden syrup is a grand thing to pour on breakfast.

clue.text: Chopper making my heart shift?

clue.text: Supreme commander has little time, once surrounded

parts.note: C-in-C is Commander-in-Chief

to end is to culminate

clue.text: A large bird I see nesting — successful result of this?

parts.note: a vulture is a large bird
the letter C sounds like see

clue.text: Rate mess appalling in sewer
